# uem_profile (Resource)

Manages a Workspace ONE UEM Profile

## Update behaviour

An update reads the live profile first and changes only what this resource manages. Payload sections and General settings the schema does not cover (for example Email and SSO payloads, or the removal password) are kept as they are in UEM.

- The configuration is the source of truth for the blocks and lists this resource manages (`description`, `passcode`, `restrictions`, `disk_encryption`, `gatekeeper`, `network_list`, `credentials_list`, `custom_settings_list`, `system_extensions`, `privacy_preferences`, `scep_list`, `web_clips_list`, `vpn_list`, `eas_microsoft_outlook`, `kernel_extension`, `custom_attributes`). Removing a block or list from the configuration deletes that payload from the profile at the next apply; removing an entry from a configured list removes that entry.
- A macOS profile must keep at least one payload: UEM rejects an update that would leave it with none, so the last managed block cannot be removed while the profile has no other payloads.
- Exceptions kept from the live profile: the Android long and short support messages; and for each `credentials_list` entry that matches exactly one live credential of the same source type (by certificate ID, else by certificate authority and template, else by name), that credential's certificate and identity preferences, plus its certificate metadata when the certificate ID is unchanged. Unmatched or ambiguous entries keep nothing from the live profile.
- UEM returns encrypted settings as `*****`. If a setting this resource does not manage comes back masked, the update is refused, because sending it would overwrite the secret with the mask. The check covers every live credential's kept settings, including credentials the configuration removes. A setting whose real value is literally `*****` is also refused, since it cannot be told apart from a masked secret. Update such profiles in the UEM console.
- If the live profile cannot be read, the update is aborted.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example Workspace ONE UEM Profile Resource

# Basic Android Profile with Lock Screen Message
resource "uem_profile" "android_basic" {
  name            = "Android Basic Profile"
  description     = "Basic Android profile created by Terraform"
  platform        = "Android"
  org_group_id    = "12345" # Replace with your Organization Group ID
  assignment_type = "Auto"
  profile_scope   = "Production"
  is_active       = true

  lock_screen_message = "Welcome to Workspace ONE UEM"
}

# iOS Profile
resource "uem_profile" "ios_basic" {
  name            = "iOS Basic Profile"
  description     = "Basic iOS profile created by Terraform"
  platform        = "Apple iOS"
  org_group_id    = "12345" # Replace with your Organization Group ID
  assignment_type = "Auto"
  profile_scope   = "Production"
  is_active       = true
}

# Windows 10 Profile
resource "uem_profile" "windows_basic" {
  name            = "Windows 10 Basic Profile"
  description     = "Basic Windows 10 profile created by Terraform"
  platform        = "Windows 10"
  org_group_id    = "12345" # Replace with your Organization Group ID
  assignment_type = "Optional"
  profile_scope   = "Staging"
  is_active       = false
}

# macOS Profile
resource "uem_profile" "macos_basic" {
  name            = "macOS Basic Profile"
  description     = "Basic macOS profile created by Terraform"
  platform        = "AppleOsX"
  org_group_id    = "12345" # Replace with your Organization Group ID
  assignment_type = "Auto"
  profile_scope   = "Production"
  is_active       = true
}

# Output the created profile IDs
output "android_profile_id" {
  description = "The ID of the Android profile"
  value       = uem_profile.android_basic.id
}

output "android_profile_uuid" {
  description = "The UUID of the Android profile"
  value       = uem_profile.android_basic.uuid
}

output "ios_profile_id" {
  description = "The ID of the iOS profile"
  value       = uem_profile.ios_basic.id
}
```

### macOS: consolidated payload example

One macOS profile combining `network_list`, `credentials_list`, `vpn_list`, `scep_list`,
`web_clips_list`, `kernel_extension` and `disk_encryption`. Write-only secrets (here, the
VPN password) come from `local.secrets[...]`, the same reference `ws1-tf onboard` generates
into a `secrets.tf`/`secrets.json` pair next to the resource — see the CLI's onboarding docs
for how that file is produced and filled in.

```terraform
locals {
  secrets = {
    "uem_profile.macos_consolidated.vpn_list[\"Corp VPN\"].password" = ""
  }
}

resource "uem_profile" "macos_consolidated" {
  name            = "macOS Consolidated Payload Example"
  description     = "Illustrates network, credential, VPN, SCEP, web clip, kernel extension and disk encryption payloads together"
  platform        = "AppleOsX"
  org_group_id    = "12345" # Replace with your Organization Group ID
  assignment_type = "Auto"
  profile_scope   = "Production"
  is_active       = true

  credentials_list = [
    {
      credential_source     = "DefinedCA"
      credential_name       = "Corp CA Cert"
      certificate_authority = 1 # Replace with your UEM Certificate Authority ID
      certificate_template  = 1 # Replace with your CA's certificate template ID
    },
  ]

  network_list = [
    {
      network_interface      = "BuiltInWireless"
      service_set_identifier = "Corp-WiFi"
      security_type          = "WPA2"
      identity_certificate   = "Corp CA Cert" # matches credentials_list[0].credential_name
      hidden_network         = false
      auto_join              = true
    },
  ]

  vpn_list = [
    {
      connection_name = "Corp VPN"
      connection_type = "L2TP"
      server          = "vpn.example.com"
      account         = "{DeviceUid}"
      password        = local.secrets["uem_profile.macos_consolidated.vpn_list[\"Corp VPN\"].password"] != "" ? local.secrets["uem_profile.macos_consolidated.vpn_list[\"Corp VPN\"].password"] : null
      proxy           = "None"
    },
  ]

  scep_list = [
    {
      name                     = "Device Identity"
      certificate_authority_id = 1 # Replace with your UEM Certificate Authority ID
      certificate_template_id  = 1 # Replace with your CA's certificate template ID
      credential_source        = "DefinedCA"
      identity_preference = {
        names = [] # known issue above: set explicitly, don't omit
      }
    },
  ]

  web_clips_list = [
    {
      label               = "Company Portal"
      url                 = "https://example.com/portal"
      show_in_app_catalog = true
    },
  ]

  kernel_extension = {
    allow_user_overrides     = false
    allowed_team_identifiers = ["ABCDE12345"]
    allowed_kernel_extensions = [
      {
        bundle_identifier = "com.example.kext"
        team_identifier   = "ABCDE12345"
      },
    ]
  }

  disk_encryption = {
    filevault2 = {
      enable                        = true
      filevault_user                = 1 # Current or Next Login User
      prompt_to_enable_filevault_at = 2 # Logout Only
      recovery_type                 = 1 # Personal
      show_recovery_key             = true
    }
    airwatch = {
      use_intelligent_hub = false
      store_key           = true
    }
  }
}
```

### macOS: Exchange (Outlook) payload example

`eas_microsoft_outlook` must be the only payload in its profile: UEM rejects a profile that
combines it with any other payload.

```terraform
resource "uem_profile" "macos_eas_outlook" {
  name            = "macOS Exchange (Outlook) Profile"
  description     = "eas_microsoft_outlook must be the only payload in its profile"
  platform        = "AppleOsX"
  org_group_id    = "12345" # Replace with your Organization Group ID
  assignment_type = "Auto"
  profile_scope   = "Production"
  is_active       = true

  eas_microsoft_outlook = {
    account_name  = "Corp Exchange"
    email_address = "{EmailAddress}"
    user_name     = "{EmailUserName}"
    exchange_host = "outlook.example.com"
    use_ssl       = true
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Profile name
- `org_group_id` (String) Organization Group ID. Must be numeric: UEM's General.ManagedLocationGroupID is a non-nullable field sent on every profile write, for every platform, so a non-numeric value is rejected at plan time rather than silently omitted from the request.
- `platform` (String) Platform: Android, Apple iOS, AppleOsX, Windows 10, Windows_Rugged, or Linux

### Optional

- `assigned_smart_groups` (List of String) List of SmartGroup IDs to assign to this profile.
- `assignment_type` (String) Assignment type: Auto, Custom, Optional, Interactive, or Compliance (case-insensitive). Defaults to Auto. Note: the Windows 10 (WinRT) platform rejects "Custom" — use one of the other 4 values there. Note: for Android profiles with provisioning enabled, UEM silently forces this to "Auto" and clears smart groups regardless of what is configured here; this is existing server behavior, not a provider validation.
- `custom_attributes` (Attributes List) macOS Custom Attributes payload (UEM `CustomAttributes`): scripts that report device attributes. `attribute_script` is the base64 script body. Values are passed to UEM and read back as-is. Applies to macOS only. A field you leave unset takes the value UEM reports (UEM fills a default for most fields on create); removing a field from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change a field set it explicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--custom_attributes))
- `credentials_list` (Attributes List) Credential payloads for macOS profiles. Each entry either uploads a certificate file (credential_source = "Upload") or references a pre-configured Certificate Authority (credential_source = "DefinedCA"). Reference a credential in a network_list entry via identity_certificate = <credential_name>. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials_list))
- `custom_settings_list` (Attributes List) Custom settings payloads (macOS, iOS, and Android). Each item contains an XML/plist custom settings string. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--custom_settings_list))
- `description` (String) Profile description. Unknown on create; on update, keeps a prior null or empty value, and clears to "" when a previously non-empty description is removed.
- `disk_encryption` (Attributes) Disk encryption (FileVault 2) settings (macOS only) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--disk_encryption))
- `excluded_smart_groups` (List of String) List of SmartGroup IDs to exclude from this profile.
- `eas_microsoft_outlook` (Attributes) macOS Exchange (Microsoft Outlook) payload (UEM `EasMicrosoftOutlook`). Values are passed to UEM and read back as-is, except `password`: UEM returns it masked, so it is write-only and never read back. UEM clears one of these secrets when an update leaves it out, so a plan that would leave out a secret UEM holds is refused: set it in the configuration first. Applies to macOS only. UEM rejects a profile that combines this payload with any other payload (HTTP 422 "Cannot add multiple payloads when AppleOsXEasMicrosoftOutlookPayloadEntity is provided", live-confirmed): put it in a profile of its own. A field you leave unset takes the value UEM reports (UEM fills a default for most fields on create); removing a field from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change a field set it explicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--eas_microsoft_outlook))
- `gatekeeper` (Attributes) macOS Security & Privacy payload (called GateKeeper in the WS1 API). Controls auto-unlock, Touch ID, Handoff, screen capture, and software update deferral. Applies to macOS only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--gatekeeper))
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the profile is active. Defaults to true
- `kernel_extension` (Attributes) macOS Kernel Extensions payload (UEM `KernelExtension`): the legacy kernel extension allow-list. Values are passed to UEM and read back as-is. Applies to macOS only. A field you leave unset takes the value UEM reports (UEM fills a default for most fields on create); removing a field from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change a field set it explicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--kernel_extension))
- `lock_screen_message` (String) Lock screen message (Android only)
- `network_list` (Attributes List) Network (Wi-Fi / Ethernet) payloads for macOS profiles. Each item configures one network connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_list))
- `passcode` (Attributes) Passcode policy settings (macOS and iOS) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--passcode))
- `privacy_preferences` (Attributes List) macOS Privacy Preferences Policy Control (PPPC) payload. Each entry is one identity/app-scoped rule granting or denying that binary access to privacy-sensitive resources (camera, microphone, calendar, and so on) plus an optional list of Apple Events it may send to other processes. Applies to macOS only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--privacy_preferences))
- `profile_context` (String) Profile context: Device or User. Required for AppleOsX profiles (defaults to Device). UEM has no server default for this field and rejects a profile without it; the provider supplies Device when it is unset.
- `profile_scope` (String) Profile scope: Production, Staging, or Both (case-insensitive), or empty. When unset, nothing is sent and UEM's own default applies (UEM stores an empty value); an update keeps the stored value. An explicit value is always sent. Some platforms (Android) need an explicit value on create. Unlike assignment_type, the casing you configure is not preserved across a refresh.
- `restrictions` (Attributes) Restrictions settings (macOS only) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--restrictions))
- `scep_list` (Attributes List) macOS SCEP payloads (UEM `ScepList`). Each entry requests a certificate from a certificate authority UEM already knows (`certificate_authority_id` and `certificate_template_id` are that CA's and template's ids in UEM; this provider doesn't manage them). Values are passed to UEM and read back as-is. Applies to macOS only. A field you leave unset takes the value UEM reports (UEM fills a default for most fields on create); removing a field from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change a field set it explicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scep_list))
- `system_extensions` (Attributes) macOS System Extensions payload. Controls whether users may approve additional system extensions on their own, plus two independent allow-lists: extension TYPES permitted for a team identifier, and specific extensions (by bundle/team identifier) always approved. Distinct from the older kernel extension payload (`kernel_extension`). Applies to macOS only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--system_extensions))
- `vpn_list` (Attributes List) macOS VPN payloads (UEM `VpnList`). Values are passed to UEM and read back as-is, except `password`, `shared_secret` and `vpn_password`: UEM returns those masked, so they are write-only and never read back. UEM clears one of these secrets when an update leaves it out, so a plan that would leave out a secret UEM holds is refused: set it in the configuration first. Applies to macOS only. A field you leave unset takes the value UEM reports (UEM fills a default for most fields on create); removing a field from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change a field set it explicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vpn_list))
- `web_clips_list` (Attributes List) macOS Web Clips (UEM `WebClipsList`): links to web pages placed on the device. Values are passed to UEM and read back as-is. Applies to macOS only. A field you leave unset takes the value UEM reports (UEM fills a default for most fields on create); removing a field from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change a field set it explicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--web_clips_list))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Profile ID
- `uuid` (String) Profile UUID

<a id="nestedatt--credentials_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credentials_list`

Required:

- `credential_source` (String) Source of the credential. Valid values: "Upload" (base64 certificate file) or "DefinedCA" (pre-configured CA in UEM) — the only value UEM's API returns for a CA-backed credential. As a provider convenience, the legacy spelling "DefinedCertificateAuthority" (from older versions of these docs) is also accepted and mapped to "DefinedCA"; UEM itself only uses "DefinedCA".

Optional:

- `allow_access_to_all_applications` (Boolean) When true, all apps on the device can access the private key in the Keychain. UEM echoes this back (false when unset), so it is read back from UEM rather than left null.
- `certificate_authority` (Number) Numeric ID of the Certificate Authority in UEM. Required when credential_source is "DefinedCA". UEM echoes this back (0 when unset), so it is read back from UEM rather than left null.
- `certificate_id` (Number) Numeric certificate ID assigned by UEM after upload. Computed automatically when credential_source is "Upload"; leave unset for DefinedCA.
- `certificate_password` (String, Sensitive) Password protecting the certificate file. Required for encrypted .pfx/.p12 files.
- `certificate_payload` (String, Sensitive) Base64-encoded certificate file (.pfx, .p12, or .cer). Required when credential_source is "Upload". Use filebase64("path/to/cert.pfx") to load from disk.
- `certificate_template` (Number) Numeric ID of the certificate template within the CA. Required when credential_source is "DefinedCA". UEM echoes this back (0 when unset), so it is read back from UEM rather than left null.
- `credential_name` (String) Human-readable name for this credential, referenced by identity_certificate in network payloads. Required when credential_source is "Upload" so network_list entries can join to it; optional for DefinedCA credentials, which are identified by certificate_authority + certificate_template.
- `key_is_extractable` (Boolean) Allow export of the private key from the Keychain (macOS 10.15+). Corresponds to "Allow export of private key from Keychain" in the UI. UEM echoes this back (true when unset), so it is read back from UEM rather than left null.


<a id="nestedatt--custom_settings_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom_settings_list`

Required:

- `custom_settings` (String) Custom settings XML/plist content


<a id="nestedatt--disk_encryption"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disk_encryption`

Optional:

- `airwatch` (Attributes) AirWatch disk encryption enforcement settings. Required whenever disk_encryption is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--disk_encryption--airwatch))
- `filevault2` (Attributes) FileVault 2 encryption settings (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--disk_encryption--filevault2))
- `mcx` (Attributes) MCX disk encryption settings. UEM's DiskEncryption ctor always instantiates a non-null MCX sub-object with its own defaults, even when this whole block is left out of the configuration, so a field you leave unset takes the value UEM reports. Removing this block from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change a field set it explicitly. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--disk_encryption--mcx))

<a id="nestedatt--disk_encryption--airwatch"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disk_encryption.airwatch`

Optional:

- `enable_recovery_key` (Boolean) Prompt for user password to rotate recovery key. Requires use_intelligent_hub = true and store_key = true. Gates the recovery_key_notification_*/recovery_key_prompt_*/recovery_key_success_*/recovery_key_error_* fields: forbidden when this is not true, all required together when this is true. UEM silently resets this to false on save whenever filevault2.recovery_type is 2 (Corporate) -- if this is left unset, the provider plans it as false to match, so an omitted value and an explicit false behave identically here.
- `encryption_action_after_last_notification` (Number) Action after last notification dismissal: 1 = Force Logout, 2 = Do Nothing. Requires notify_user_for_encryption = true.
- `encryption_max_notify_attempts` (Number) Maximum times to show the encryption notification (0-100). Requires notify_user_for_encryption = true.
- `encryption_notification_message` (String) Message for the encryption notification. Requires notify_user_for_encryption = true.
- `encryption_notification_retry_interval_in_hours` (Number) Retry interval in hours between notification dismissals (1-168). Requires notify_user_for_encryption = true.
- `encryption_notification_title` (String) Title for the encryption notification (max 29 chars). Requires notify_user_for_encryption = true.
- `notify_user_for_encryption` (Boolean) Notify user if encryption is disabled. Requires use_intelligent_hub = true. Gates the encryption_notification_*/encryption_max_notify_attempts/encryption_action_after_last_notification fields: forbidden when this is not true, all required together when this is true.
- `recovery_key_error_message` (String) Error message for recovery key rotation failure (max 150 chars). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_error_title` (String) Error title for recovery key rotation failure (max 50 chars). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_max_failure_count` (Number) Maximum times to retry recovery key rotation on failure (1-5).
- `recovery_key_notification_message` (String) Message for rotating recovery key notification. Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_notification_retry_interval_in_hours` (Number) Retry interval in hours for recovery key notification (1-168). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_notification_title` (String) Title for rotating recovery key notification (max 29 chars). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_prompt_message` (String) Prompt message for rotating recovery key (max 150 chars). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_prompt_title` (String) Prompt title for rotating recovery key (max 50 chars). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_success_message` (String) Success message after recovery key rotation (max 150 chars). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `recovery_key_success_title` (String) Success title after recovery key rotation (max 50 chars). Requires enable_recovery_key = true.
- `rotate_key_after` (Number) Days until the recovery key rotates. Not validated by UEM.
- `store_key` (Boolean) Store the recovery key in AirWatch. Required when filevault2.recovery_type is 1 (Personal) or 3 (Personal and Corporate); forbidden when recovery_type is 2 (Corporate). Required (true) when enable_recovery_key is true.
- `use_intelligent_hub` (Boolean) Use Intelligent Hub for enforcement. Required whenever disk_encryption is configured. When true, at least one of notify_user_for_encryption or enable_recovery_key must also be true (both must be set, and not both false).


<a id="nestedatt--disk_encryption--filevault2"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disk_encryption.filevault2`

Optional:

- `enable` (Boolean) Enforce disk encryption. Must be true whenever disk_encryption is configured; UEM rejects an explicit false at apply time. UEM's FileVault2 ctor defaults this to true (a non-nullable bool) whenever it is left unset, so an omitted value takes that default rather than planning null. Removing it from the configuration keeps its current value rather than clearing it, so to change it set it explicitly.
- `filevault_enterprise_certificate` (String) credential_name of a credentials_list entry in this same profile, used for institutional recovery. Required when recovery_type is 2 (Corporate) or 3 (Personal and Corporate); forbidden when recovery_type is 1 (Personal).
- `filevault_user` (Number) User type added to FileVault: 1 = Current or Next Login User, 2 = Specific User. Required whenever disk_encryption is configured.
- `number_of_times_user_can_bypass` (Number) Number of times user can bypass the FileVault prompt (0-10). Required when prompt_to_enable_filevault_at is 1 (Both Login and Logout) or 3 (Login Only); forbidden when prompt_to_enable_filevault_at is 2 (Logout Only).
- `prompt_to_enable_filevault_at` (Number) When to prompt: 1 = Both Login and Logout, 2 = Logout Only, 3 = Login Only. Required whenever disk_encryption is configured. 1 and 3 require number_of_times_user_can_bypass; 2 forbids it.
- `recovery_type` (Number) Recovery type: 1 = Personal, 2 = Corporate, 3 = Personal and Corporate. Required whenever disk_encryption is configured. 2 or 3 require filevault_enterprise_certificate; 1 forbids it.
- `show_recovery_key` (Boolean) Show the personal recovery key to the user. Required when recovery_type is 1 (Personal) or 3 (Personal and Corporate); forbidden when recovery_type is 2 (Corporate).
- `username` (String) Open Directory username for FileVault. Required when filevault_user = 2 (Specific User); forbidden otherwise.


<a id="nestedatt--disk_encryption--mcx"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disk_encryption.mcx`

Optional:

- `destroy_fv_key_on_standby` (Boolean) Require user to unlock disk after hibernation. Left unset, UEM reports its own default (live-confirmed: false) rather than leaving the field genuinely absent.



<a id="nestedatt--gatekeeper"></a>
### Nested Schema for `gatekeeper`

Optional:

- `allow_auto_unlock` (Boolean) If false, disallows macOS auto unlock with Apple Watch (defaults to true).
- `allow_fingerprint_for_unlock` (Boolean) If false, prevents Touch ID from unlocking a device.
- `allow_handoff` (Boolean) If false, disables activity continuation features in macOS.
- `allow_screen_capture` (Boolean) If false, users can't save a screenshot of the display and are prevented from capturing a screen recording; it also prevents the Classroom app from observing remote screens.
- `enable_app_software_update_delay` (Boolean) Enable delay for non-OS app software updates.
- `enable_software_update_delay` (Boolean) Enable delay for OS software updates.
- `enforced_software_update_delay` (Number) Number of days a software update on the device is delayed (default 30 once a delay toggle is enabled).


<a id="nestedatt--network_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_list`

~> `trusted_certificates` is not yet proven live when omitted on create: if UEM echoes a non-empty default, the create could fail with an inconsistent result. Set it explicitly (e.g. `[]`) as a workaround.

Optional:

- `allow_trust_exceptions` (Boolean) Allow dynamic trust decisions by the user
- `allow_two_rands` (Boolean) Allow two RANDs for EAP-SIM authentication
- `auto_join` (Boolean) Automatically join this network
- `disable_association_mac_randomization` (Boolean) Disable MAC address randomization when associating with this network
- `eap_aka` (Boolean) Use EAP-AKA for authentication
- `eap_fast` (Boolean) Use EAP-FAST for authentication
- `eap_sim` (Boolean) Use EAP-SIM for authentication
- `hidden_network` (Boolean) Whether the network is hidden (not broadcasting SSID)
- `identity_certificate` (String) Name of the credential from credentials_list to use as the EAP identity certificate. Must match the credential_name of a credentials_list entry.
- `inner_identity` (String) Inner authentication method used by TTLS. Must be one of: "PAP", "CHAP", "MSCHAP", "MSCHAPv2" (exact match). Required when ttls = true.
- `leap` (Boolean) Use LEAP for EAP authentication
- `network_interface` (String) Network interface. Must be one of: "BuiltInWireless", "FirstActiveEthernet", "SecondActiveEthernet", "ThirdActiveEthernet", "FirstEthernet", "SecondEthernet", "ThirdEthernet", "AnyEthernet" (exact match; UEM rejects any other value, e.g. "Wi-Fi", with a 422). When "BuiltInWireless", security_type must also be set.
- `outer_identity` (String) Outer identity for TTLS, PEAP, and EAP-FAST (hides real identity)
- `pac_fallback` (Boolean) Allow direct connection if the PAC file is unreachable
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Pre-shared key (PSK) password for the network
- `peap` (Boolean) Use PEAP for EAP authentication
- `proxy_password` (String, Sensitive) Password for proxy authentication
- `proxy_server` (String) Hostname of the HTTP proxy server
- `proxy_server_port` (Number) Port number of the HTTP proxy server
- `proxy_type` (String) Proxy type (e.g. None, Manual, Auto)
- `proxy_url` (String) URL of the proxy auto-configuration (PAC) file
- `proxy_username` (String) Username for proxy authentication
- `security_type` (String) Encryption type of the Wi-Fi network (e.g. WPA2, WPA3, WEP, None). Required when network_interface = "BuiltInWireless".
- `service_set_identifier` (String) SSID of the Wi-Fi network
- `tls` (Boolean) Use TLS for EAP authentication
- `tls_maximum_version` (String) Maximum TLS version for EAP-TLS (default 1.2)
- `tls_minimum_version` (String) Minimum TLS version for EAP-TLS (default 1.0)
- `trusted_certificates` (List of String) List of trusted certificate names for EAP authentication
- `ttls` (Boolean) Use TTLS for EAP authentication
- `use_as_login_window_configuration` (Boolean) Allow user to authenticate to the network at login (macOS)
- `use_directory_authentication` (Boolean) Use the machine's directory credentials for authentication (macOS)
- `use_pac` (Boolean) Use an existing PAC (Protected Access Credential) if present
- `user_name` (String) Username for EAP authentication
- `user_password` (String, Sensitive) Password for EAP authentication


<a id="nestedatt--passcode"></a>
### Nested Schema for `passcode`

Optional:

- `allow_simple_value` (Boolean) Allow simple passcode values
- `auto_lock` (String) Auto-lock timeout (in minutes)
- `grace_period` (Number) Grace period before requiring passcode (in minutes)
- `max_failed_attempts` (String) Maximum number of failed passcode attempts. iOS accepts the sentinel "None" meaning no limit; both iOS and macOS accept numeric strings in the documented range.
- `maximum_passcode_age` (String) Maximum passcode age (in days)
- `minimum_number_of_complex_characters` (String) Minimum number of complex characters
- `minimum_passcode_length` (Number) Minimum passcode length
- `minutes_until_failed_login_reset` (Number) Minutes until failed login attempt counter resets
- `pin_history` (String) Number of previous PINs to remember (numeric string, 1-50). Stored as a string to match the iOS canonical API type.
- `require_alphanumeric_value` (Boolean) Require alphanumeric passcode
- `require_passcode_on_device` (Boolean) Require passcode on the device


<a id="nestedatt--privacy_preferences"></a>
### Nested Schema for `privacy_preferences`

Required:

- `identifier` (String) Bundle ID or install path of the target binary this rule applies to.
- `identifier_type` (String) How to interpret identifier. Must be either "bundleID" or "path".

Optional:

- `accessibility` (String) Access to control the computer via Accessibility APIs. Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".
- `address_book` (String) Access to Contacts. Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".
- `apple_events_list` (Attributes List) Specific Apple Event receivers this identity is allowed (or denied) to send events to. UEM folds an identity-level Apple Events receiver into this list on write and never returns it in the older identity-level form, so this is the only supported way to configure Apple Events for a rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--privacy_preferences--apple_events_list))
- `calendar` (String) Access to Calendar. Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".
- `camera` (String) Access to the camera. Can only be "Disallow" -- access cannot be granted by a profile.
- `code_requirement` (String) Code signing requirement for identifier (the output of `codesign -d -r-`).
- `comment` (String) Freeform note about this rule.
- `file_provider_presence` (String) Access to File Provider presence. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `listen_event` (String) Access to listen for system-wide keyboard/mouse events. Can only be "Disallow".
- `media_library` (String) Access to the Media Library. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `microphone` (String) Access to the microphone. Can only be "Disallow" -- access cannot be granted by a profile.
- `photos` (String) Access to Photos. Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".
- `post_event` (String) Access to post synthesized system-wide keyboard/mouse events. Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".
- `reminders` (String) Access to Reminders. Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".
- `screen_capture` (String) Access to capture the screen. Can only be "Disallow".
- `speech_recognition` (String) Access to Speech Recognition. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `static_code` (Boolean) Whether identifier's code requirement should be evaluated statically rather than at runtime.
- `system_policy_all_files` (String) Full Disk Access. Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".
- `system_policy_desktop_folder` (String) Access to the Desktop folder. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `system_policy_documents_folder` (String) Access to the Documents folder. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `system_policy_downloads_folder` (String) Access to the Downloads folder. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `system_policy_network_volumes` (String) Access to network-mounted volumes. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `system_policy_removable_volumes` (String) Access to removable volumes. Accepted values are not restated by the SDK doc comment and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.
- `system_policy_sys_admin_files` (String) Access to administer the system (files normally requiring elevated privileges). Must be either "Allow" or "Disallow".

<a id="nestedatt--privacy_preferences--apple_events_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `privacy_preferences.apple_events_list`

Optional:

- `code_requirement` (String) Code signing requirement for this Apple Event receiver.
- `identifier` (String) Bundle ID or install path of this Apple Event receiver.
- `identifier_type` (String) How to interpret identifier. Must be either "bundleID" or "path".
- `permission` (String) Whether this identity may send Apple Events to this receiver. Accepted values are not documented by the SDK and unconfirmed live; left unvalidated.

<a id="nestedatt--system_extensions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `system_extensions`

Optional:

- `allow_user_overrides` (Boolean) If false, restricts users from approving additional system extensions on their own.
- `allowed_system_extension_types` (Attributes List) Extension TYPES (driver, endpoint security, network) allowed for a given team identifier, without naming a specific extension. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--system_extensions--allowed_system_extension_types))
- `allowed_system_extensions` (Attributes List) Specific system extensions, by bundle and/or team identifier, that are always approved on the machine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--system_extensions--allowed_system_extensions))

<a id="nestedatt--system_extensions--allowed_system_extension_types"></a>
### Nested Schema for `system_extensions.allowed_system_extension_types`

Required:

- `team_identifier` (String) Apple Developer Team ID this rule applies to, or "*" for the global team identifier.

Optional:

- `allow_driver_extension_type` (Boolean) Allow driver extension type for this team identifier.
- `allow_endpoint_security_extension_type` (Boolean) Allow endpoint security extension type for this team identifier.
- `allow_network_extension_type` (Boolean) Allow network extension type for this team identifier.

~> UEM automatically adds a `"*"` (global team identifier) entry with all three types denied, representing its implicit deny-all-others default, alongside any team-specific entries you configure. The provider drops this server-added entry on read so it never shows up as configuration drift. If you want to manage the `"*"` entry explicitly (for example to allow a type for every team), configure it yourself and the provider will keep and manage it like any other entry. A `"*"` entry that allows any extension type is never treated as the server default, so it is always kept in state (for example when importing a profile whose `"*"` entry was set in the console).

<a id="nestedatt--system_extensions--allowed_system_extensions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `system_extensions.allowed_system_extensions`

Optional:

- `bundle_identifier` (String) Bundle identifier of the system extension to always approve.
- `team_identifier` (String) Apple Developer Team ID of the system extension to always approve.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash
# Import an existing Workspace ONE profile into Terraform state

# Import by profile ID and platform
# Usage: terraform import uem_profile.example "<profile_id>:<platform>"

terraform import uem_profile.android_basic "12345:Android"
```

<a id="nestedatt--custom_attributes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom_attributes`

~> Creating a macOS Custom Attributes payload isn't supported in 26.2: with a script, UEM re-encodes it; without script, schedule and events, UEM created a profile it then couldn't read back (HTTP 500). Importing profiles with custom attributes but no script works; `ws1-tf onboard` refuses ones with a script.

Optional:

- `attribute_name` (String) Attribute name (UEM `AttributeName`).
- `attribute_script` (String) Attribute script (UEM `AttributeScript`).
- `events` (List of String) Events (UEM `Events`).
- `schedule` (Number) Schedule (UEM `Schedule`).
